rows.definition: gateway.Server.AdjudicateAssistantTurn runs every tool call a BUFFERED assistant turn proposes through the served chat floor and rewrites the message in place: only admitted calls survive, refusal or served-inline text is folded into Content, and it returns the OpenAI finish_reason plus one ToolAdjudication per proposed call.
rows.distinction: It is the per-TURN entry point over a whole buffered assistant message, not the adjudicator itself (the pre-call reference monitor that decides one call), and not its streamed twin AdjudicateStreamedToolCalls, which cannot blank prose already on the wire.

rows.definition: gateway.Server.AdjudicateStreamedToolCalls is the streamed twin of AdjudicateAssistantTurn: it adjudicates the tool calls of a turn whose prose has already been streamed, blanks nothing, and returns a StreamedToolAdjudication whose Trailer carries the refusal or served-inline text the stream appends.
rows.distinction: It adjudicates STREAMED calls after the prose is on the wire (append a trailer), unlike AdjudicateAssistantTurn, which rewrites a buffered message in place; neither is the adjudicator, which decides a single call.

rows.definition: gateway.Server.applyAdjudicatedTurn folds one already-adjudicated proposal set into the assistant message the OpenAI wire carries (refused-body blanking, vDSO served-inline text, the livelock advisory note) and returns the finish_reason: tool_calls while calls survive, stop when every proposal was refused or served inline, else the upstream finish.
rows.distinction: It APPLIES verdicts that were already reached to the wire message; it decides nothing. Deciding is the adjudicator's job, and AdjudicateAssistantTurn is the caller that both decides and then applies.

rows.definition: turnkeyServer.toolAdjudicator (cmd/fak) returns the gateway.Server that adjudicates the fak up server's proposed tool calls; a server built outside startTurnkeyServer shares one lazily built process default, so no construction path returns a proposed call unadjudicated.
rows.distinction: It is a fak up ACCESSOR that hands back the gateway doing the adjudication (toolAdjudicatOR, a provider), not ToolAdjudicatION, the per-call decision record that gateway produces, and not the adjudicator itself (the reference monitor inside that gateway); it exists so fak up applies the same served chat floor as serve.

rows.definition: writeTurnkeyAdjudicationUnavailable (cmd/fak) writes the HTTP 502 server_error JSON body fak up returns when its tool adjudicator cannot be built, so a turn with proposed tool calls fails closed rather than reaching the client unadjudicated.
rows.distinction: It reports that ADJUDICATION ITSELF IS UNAVAILABLE (an infrastructure failure, 502), not a refusal verdict: a denied call is an adjudicator decision folded into the turn by applyAdjudicatedTurn, while this path means no decision could be made.
